articles.title: EarnIn Secures Additional $150 Million Debt Facility
articles.snippet:
EarnIn has secured a new $150 million committed warehouse facility from a major Canadian financial institution, expanding the company's access to institutional financing as it continues to scale its earnings management and payroll platform.
The post EarnIn Secures Additional $150 Million Debt Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
EarnIn Secures Additional $150 Million Debt Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
EarnIn Secures Additional $150 Million Debt Facility
EarnIn has secured a new $150 million committed warehouse facility from a major Canadian financial institution, expanding the company’s access to institutional financing as it continues to scale its earnings management and payroll platform.
The new facility represents an additional source of committed debt capital for EarnIn and further diversifies the group of financial institutions supporting the company.
Combined with EarnIn’s existing debt investors, the facility increases the company’s total financing capacity to more than $500 million.
EarnIn plans to use the additional borrowing capacity to support its long-term growth strategy and continued expansion across its product portfolio.
The financing provides the company with additional capital flexibility as it works to broaden the services available to workers and employers through its technology platform.
EarnIn develops earnings management and payroll software intended to give workers greater control over when and how they receive money they have already earned.
Its offerings include products providing on-demand earnings and early access to earnings, allowing eligible workers to access compensation on a schedule that more closely matches their individual financial needs.
The company’s broader portfolio also includes Earn Better by EarnIn and EarnIn Payroll, extending EarnIn’s business beyond its core earnings access capabilities.
As EarnIn’s product suite expands, the company is building a broader platform around the movement and management of employee earnings.
The latest warehouse facility provides additional capacity to support that growth while reducing EarnIn’s reliance on any single source of institutional financing.
Bringing a major Canadian financial institution into EarnIn’s lender group also expands the company’s relationships with international banking partners.
EarnIn believes the more diversified lender base will provide greater flexibility and resiliency as the business grows.
The additional financing capacity is also expected to lower EarnIn’s overall cost of capital, potentially providing the company with more efficient funding as it continues investing in its products and scaling its operations.
With more than $500 million of total financing capacity now available through its debt investors, EarnIn has increased the financial resources available to support continued development of its earnings management and payroll offerings.
The facility represents another step in the company’s strategy to build a diversified institutional capital base that can support longer-term growth.
KEY QUOTE:
“Building a diversified capital base gives us greater flexibility and resiliency as we scale. Adding a major international banking partner strengthens our lender base and lowers our cost of capital, positioning EarnIn for continued growth.”
Jacopo Lenzi, Chief Financial Officer of EarnIn

articles.title: Everforth ECS Secures $148 Million SUNet Contract Extension
articles.snippet:
Everforth ECS has secured a three-year sole-source contract expansion with a ceiling of $148 million to continue supporting the Chief Digital and AI Office's Secure Unclassified Network while also developing next-generation capabilities for SUNet 2.0.
The post Everforth ECS Secures $148 Million SUNet Contract Extension appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Everforth ECS Secures $148 Million SUNet Contract Extension
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Everforth ECS Secures $148 Million SUNet Contract Extension
Everforth ECS has secured a three-year sole-source contract expansion with a $148 million ceiling to continue supporting the Chief Digital and AI Office’s Secure Unclassified Network while developing next-generation capabilities for SUNet 2.0.
The indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity award extends Everforth ECS support for the program for more than a decade.
The company was separately selected through a Commercial Solutions Opening to research and prototype SUNet 2.0 for the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and the Chief Digital and AI Office.
Under the expanded SUNet contract, Everforth ECS will continue operating and maintaining the existing environment while supporting migration of mission capabilities to future architecture.
SUNet 2.0 is intended to provide Department of War organizations and mission partners with a secure digital environment for collaborating and rapidly developing, testing and validating AI and machine learning capabilities.
The modernization effort will explore hybrid cloud infrastructure, zero-trust security controls and modern data management capabilities.
Everforth ECS said those technologies are intended to reduce the time required to onboard users and move new capabilities toward operational deployment.
The company will simultaneously sustain the current SUNet environment for existing users while developing SUNet 2.0 as a secure experimentation environment.
KEY QUOTES:
“These awards represent the next chapter of a mission we have supported alongside the Department of War and its mission partners for more than a decade. While we continue to keep SUNet secure and responsive to the mission, we will also help transition to what comes next. By bringing our operational knowledge together with modern cloud, cybersecurity, automation, and AI capabilities, we can provide CDAO and its mission partners a faster, more secure way to experiment, collaborate, and turn emerging technologies into operational capability.”
Donnie Scott, President of Everforth ECS
“Our many years supporting SUNet have taught us our users’ challenges, what they’re constrained by, and what actually moves their mission forward. That experience is shaping every part of this modernization, with the goal of giving mission partners a faster, more secure way to test, integrate, and operationalize emerging capabilities.”
Brian Orsi, CDAO Account Lead at Everforth ECS

articles.title: Barings Provides $138.6 Million Mortgage Financing To Refinance Speedway Commerce Center
articles.snippet:
Barings has provided $138.6 million in first mortgage financing to refinance Speedway Commerce Center, a two-building Class A industrial property in Rancho Cucamonga, California.
The post Barings Provides $138.6 Million Mortgage Financing To Refinance Speedway Commerce Center appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Barings Provides $138.6 Million Mortgage Financing To Refinance Speedway Commerce Center
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Barings Provides $138.6 Million Mortgage Financing To Refinance Speedway Commerce Center
Barings has provided $138.6 million in first mortgage financing to refinance Speedway Commerce Center, a two-building Class A industrial property in Rancho Cucamonga, California.
The financing was provided to Hillwood, an industrial real estate developer and investor with operations across North America and Europe. Speedway Commerce Center consists of two recently constructed industrial buildings totaling approximately 656,000 square feet.
The property is currently 100% leased and includes modern logistics and distribution features such as high clear heights, extensive loading infrastructure, and significant automobile and trailer parking capacity.
Speedway Commerce Center is located in California’s Inland Empire, one of the country’s largest logistics and distribution markets. The property offers immediate access to Interstate 10 and Interstate 15, providing connections throughout Southern California as well as routes to the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.
The transaction expands the relationship between Barings and Hillwood. The two companies have previously worked together on industrial real estate projects in Europe, while the Speedway Commerce Center financing extends that relationship into Hillwood’s U.S. industrial portfolio.
Hillwood is a Perot Company focused on developing, acquiring, and managing institutional-grade industrial real estate. The company operates across North America and European markets including the United Kingdom, Germany, and Poland.
Barings manages approximately $500 billion in assets globally as of September 30, 2026. The alternative asset manager works with institutional, insurance, and wealth clients across credit, real assets, capital solutions, and emerging markets.
Barings is a subsidiary of MassMutual, with MS&AD holding a minority investment in the firm. The Speedway Commerce Center transaction adds to Barings’ commercial real estate lending activity and provides Hillwood with refinancing for a fully leased logistics asset in a strategically important Southern California distribution corridor.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased to provide this financing to Hillwood, a best-in-class industrial developer with a long track record of delivering high-quality logistics assets in key distribution markets. Speedway Commerce Center is a modern, strategically located industrial asset in one of the country’s most sought-after logistics markets, with excellent transportation connectivity and strong long-term demand drivers.”
Tom Cross, Managing Director At Barings
“Hillwood is pleased to extend its relationship with Barings to our US industrial business, following the firms’ work together in Europe. This financing supports the continued, efficient operation of Speedway Commerce Center and builds on Hillwood’s momentum in the Inland Empire.”
Benton Hyatt, Senior Vice President Of Debt Markets At Hillwood

articles.title: CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing
articles.snippet:
CBL Properties completed a $135 million refinancing of the mortgage loan secured by West County Center in St. Louis, addressing the company's final near-term debt maturity.
The post CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
CBL Properties Completes $135 Million West County Center Refinancing
CBL Properties completed a $135 million refinancing of the mortgage loan secured by West County Center in St. Louis, addressing the company’s final near-term debt maturity.
The new non-recourse loan replaces an existing $136.4 million mortgage that had been scheduled to mature in December 2026.
The refinancing has a five-year term and a fixed interest rate of 7.4%.
Following repayment of the existing mortgage and release of escrow balances, CBL received approximately $2 million of net proceeds.
The transaction also eliminates a cash management sweep associated with the previous loan.
CBL estimates that removing that restriction will unlock more than $7 million of annual free cash flow.
The refinancing brings CBL’s new financing activity during 2026 to nearly $1 billion.
The company said its financings this year have generated approximately $45 million of estimated incremental annual cash flow while addressing all near-term maturities.
Separately, a $22.5 million Community Improvement District bond refinancing tied to West County Center closed in September.
That transaction generated $4.6 million of cash for CBL and another $2.6 million earmarked for property improvements.
Planned projects include upgraded security cameras, escalator replacement, lighting improvements, and parking-area upgrades.
West County Center is a nearly 1.2 million-square-foot regional mall generating annual sales exceeding $900 per square foot.
Its anchors include Macy’s, Dick’s Sporting Goods, and Missouri’s only Nordstrom location.
KEY QUOTES:
“We have completed nearly $1.0 billion in new financing activity in 2026, addressing all of our near-term maturities. These financings have unlocked approximately $45.0 million in estimated incremental annual cash flow and removed maturity risk for the next few years.”
Ben Jaenicke, EVP and CFO of CBL Properties
“The terms we achieved on West County Center reflect the strong leasing and performance of the property in recent years and support the continued financial flexibility of our balance sheet.”
Ben Jaenicke, EVP and CFO of CBL Properties

articles.title: QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
articles.snippet:
QumulusAI, an Atlanta-based provider of AI cloud infrastructure, has expanded its equipment lease financing arrangement with Tech Finance Co. (TFC) to approximately $123.6 million, up from the previously announced $26 million in May 2026.
The post QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
QumulusAI, an Atlanta-based provider of AI cloud infrastructure, has expanded its equipment lease financing arrangement with Tech Finance Co. (TFC) to approximately $123.6 million, up from the previously announced $26 million in May 2026.
The expanded financing supports the acquisition and deployment of NVIDIA Blackwell graphics processing units that QumulusAI announced purchasing in May and July 2026.
The financing structure allows the company to expand its computing infrastructure without issuing additional equity, using equipment leases alongside customer deposits to fund hardware purchases.
Under the arrangement, TFC finances approximately 85% to 90% of equipment costs associated with each lease schedule. Customer deposits cover the remaining portion.
The leases have three-year terms, with amortized payment schedules implying an annualized interest rate in the high-single-digit range.
At the end of each lease term, QumulusAI has the option to purchase the underlying equipment or return it without retaining an ongoing equipment obligation.
The structure provides flexibility for managing computing hardware investments in an industry where AI accelerators are expensive and technological capabilities are evolving rapidly.
QumulusAI operates a distributed AI cloud infrastructure platform focused on providing high-performance GPU computing resources for enterprise and AI development workloads.
Its infrastructure strategy emphasizes inference-first deployments, with computing capacity installed in response to customer demand rather than relying exclusively on speculative data center expansion.
The company operates across a network of data center locations, enabling it to bring computing resources closer to customers and provide flexible alternatives to traditional centralized cloud platforms.
NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture is designed to support demanding AI workloads, including large-scale model inference and other accelerated computing applications.
For QumulusAI, the ability to obtain financing for these systems is an important component of its strategy to expand available GPU capacity while managing the substantial capital requirements associated with AI infrastructure.
The company has used a combination of customer deposits, cash generated by existing computing deployments, and financing partnerships to support its growth.
The expanded TFC relationship reinforces that approach by linking infrastructure spending to contracted demand.
Tech Finance Co. has provided equipment financing services since 2004 and began financing AI-related equipment in 2021.
The company specializes in financing structures that help businesses acquire technology infrastructure while reducing upfront capital requirements.
The $123.6 million arrangement gives QumulusAI additional capacity to deploy Blackwell-based computing resources without diluting existing shareholders through new equity issuance.
KEY QUOTES:
“We have funded our GPU deployments the same way since the start. With customer deposits, cash from capacity already in production and financing partners like TFC. Expanding this facility keeps that model in place as we scale, so the hardware is paid for by contracted demand rather than by our shareholders.”
